Flagged for review

These are the things that did not fit, did not verify, or looked wrong. They are published with the evidence so you can decide what to do with them. None of them block the site from building or publishing.

#severityfindingevidencestatus
F-01fixed A prior session reported gas prices as unverifiable. Its data file (docs/data/verified-markets.json, PR #1) recorded series KXGASPRICE as "HTTP error" and published gas as unverified. That ticker does not exist. Gas markets are the KXAAAGAS* family. live series query ↗ · archived prior file ↗ Corrected in this build; prior file archived, not deleted.
F-02fixed A prior session reported golf under series KXGOLF. No such series exists in the Sports/Golf sample. Golf is the KXPGA* and KXDPWT* families, filed under category Sports with tag Golf. live series query ↗ Corrected in this build.
F-03open Topic assignment cannot be fully official. Kalshi exposes a category and free-form tags, not a "gas prices" topic. Gas and golf need a tag match; elections, culture and crypto map 1:1 to categories. A market whose series is not in the sampled catalogue can only be assigned by ticker prefix, which is a heuristic. Every row states which basis was used. series schema ↗ Documented on every row; no silent guessing.
F-04open Culture settlement-source lists contain search-engine placeholders. Both culture series name entries such as https://www.google.com/search?q=Verge and even a truncated account holder of entry, alongside real outlets. Reproduced verbatim; not sanitised. live culture series ↗ · culture page Upstream data quality; flagged only.
F-05open Live browser access to the demo API is untested from the Pages origin. The build sandbox cannot reach Kalshi at all, so CORS and any origin restriction can only be observed in a real browser. The dashboard handles failure explicitly (snapshot + timestamp) rather than pretending to be live. test in this browser ↗ Needs a human in a browser; the failure mode is visible, not silent.
F-06open Demo liquidity is not real liquidity. Gas and election ladders held tens to a few hundred contracts with zero daily volume; several markets had nothing but a 0.00 bid and a 1.00 offer. Depth is shown as recorded, and the strategy replay skips trades instead of filling them. demo env docs ↗ · sample book ↗ Inherent to the demo environment; disclosed on the dashboard and strategies page.

It is shown as a worked example of the alert and depth machinery, labelled off-topic, and excluded from the five topic tables. series object ↗ Labelled everywhere it appears; not counted as a tracked topic.
F-08retracted Correction to my own earlier claim. I first recorded the prior session's crypto tickers as wrong (KXBTC-26NOV2201-… "should be" KXBTCD-…). That was wrong: KXBTC is a real series — a separate hourly BRTI ladder that happens to share exchange shard 2 with KXBTCD. Both tickers exist, both resolved NO, and both are now in the dataset. The prior session's actual error was narrower: merging the two families and filing a NATO Secretary-General market under Elections. The wrong claim stays visible here rather than being quietly deleted. series KXBTC ↗ · market ↗ · NATO series ↗ Retracted; KXBTC rows added to the crypto page and the resolved tracker.

Everything is simulated and labelled as such. To switch to the real demo account, add keys outside the repo and use the V2 order endpoint. balance endpoint ↗ · order v2 ↗ Documented, not worked around.
F-15open Some series ship empty or placeholder settlement-source names. KXNEXTNATOSECGEN lists entries with an empty name, the bare word agency, and long descriptive sentences in the name field, all pointing at kalshi.com. Anything keyed on source names would break; this site prints the name exactly as returned and links the URL, and infers nothing from it. series object ↗ Upstream data quality; flagged only.
F-13open The official fee schedule contradicts itself. Its prose says the fee is rounded up "to a centicent" ($0.0001), but all 21 rows of its own General Trading Fees Table match rounding up to the nearest cent. The clearest case is a $0.01 contract: the formula gives 0.07 × 100 × 0.01 × 0.99 = $0.0693, the prose rule leaves $0.0693, and the table says $0.07. This repo implements the table-consistent rule by default and exposes the prose rule as an explicit mode, so the difference is never hidden inside a P&L number. Recomputed all 21 rows: 21/21 match the cent rule, 0/21 match the centicent rule at $0.01 and $0.05. fee schedule (PDF) ↗ · check in scripts/verify_site.py: "fee model reproduces all 21 official table rows" Implemented + flagged; ask Kalshi support which rule is authoritative before trading size.

They were read but not merged; merging them would duplicate or contradict the verified data on this branch. Their claims are logged in COORDINATION.md ↗. branch list ↗ Left untouched intentionally.

How to raise one of these

Each finding lists the query that produced it. Re-run that URL, compare with the row on this page, and open an issue with the two side by side. Nothing here is worth "fixing" by editing the data file — either the API says it or it goes in this list.
